use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

evidence_cards.content: The protocols in this section are to be followed in order to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective (goal) of following the protocols described in the section, which is to minimize dual designations. This directly fills the 'goal' slot for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The primary actor (C2 JU) shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates specific conditions exist, such as Identity (ID) conflicts, different Mode II codes, or Operational Contingency Constraints (OCC).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the objective of the use case: to determine whether automatic correlation is permissible based on specific track attributes and constraints.

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to prevent or eliminate dual designations of ballistic missile tracks through the process of track correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the high-level objective (goal) of the primary actor in the context of resolving dual designations via track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is the 'DIFFERENCE RESOLUTION' of Environment/Category, Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator field values.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This text explicitly defines the high-level goal of the use case as resolving differences in specific track data fields.

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the C2 JU is to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states the objective (goal) of the primary actor (C2 JU) in this specific context.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the explicit condition required before the C2 JU can assume R² of an IU and proceed with reporting it as a track or point — thus serving as a precondition for resolving dual designations via correlation in this context.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs that have the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action shall also have the capability to deactivate this automatic capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a mandatory precondition: if the C2 JU is configured for automatic track initiation (which could lead to dual designations), it must possess the functional capability to disable that automation before or during correlation operations.

evidence_cards.content: The system must have local sensor data available for internal correlation, as the method used is a system design option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the presence of local sensor data is a fundamental state required for the correlation process to operate.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation tests require tracks and IUs (Internal Units) to be present so their positions can be extrapolated to the same time for comparison.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the necessary input entities (tracks and IUs) that must exist in the system state before the specific testing logic described in the use case can be executed.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a mandatory pre-existing system state condition regarding ID conflicts that must hold to inhibit automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a mandatory pre-existing system state condition regarding Mode II code discrepancies that must hold to inhibit automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks (i.e., being updated with local positional data).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a mandatory pre-existing system state condition regarding the source of track data (local vs remote) that must hold to inhibit automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a mandatory pre-existing system state condition regarding the Strength field value that must hold to inhibit automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory testing frequency (twice) required for two tracks to be eligible for correlation execution, establishing a precondition state.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that if ID conflicts are the sole barrier to correlation, an alert must be generated as a precondition for operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: The process of track correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data (e.g., position, velocity, boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the system must have access to both local sensor data and external interface data as a prerequisite for performing the correlation comparison.

evidence_cards.content: The recognition and resolution of dual designations require all IUs to periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the continuous system state (periodic comparison) that must be active before a specific correlation event can be recognized.

evidence_cards.content: The frequency of such comparisons, the criteria for determining that two tracks represent the same object, and the correlation rules shall be in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1, Air and Surface Track Correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that specific correlation criteria and rules must already exist/be defined in the referenced section for the process to function.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU (which includes correlating tracks) is when a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a concrete time-based event that initiates the correlation/resolution process described in the use case context.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU is when a J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a status-change event in a received message that initiates the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU is when a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a specific message type and action code that triggers the correlation assumption.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU is when the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a data quality threshold event that triggers the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the correlation process is the comparison of locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly defines the event that commences the correlation process to prevent dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the trigger event (recognition of eligibility) and the immediate required response (initiate action), which starts the use case.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific trigger condition (RV=2) that initiates a time-bound suppression of automatic correlation requests, which is part of the trigger logic for managing dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a trigger event (manual correlation rejection) that activates an operator alert, initiating human intervention in the resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU (which initiates the track correlation process) is when a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific time-based event that triggers the resolution of dual designations by assuming responsibility for a track.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU is when a J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific status change in a received message that triggers the assumption of responsibility and subsequent correlation logic.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU is when a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific command message ('Drop Track') that triggers the receiving unit to take over tracking duties.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to assume R² of an IU is when the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a data quality threshold breach that serves as a triggering condition for changing track ownership/responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the initiating event ('commences with') for the track correlation use case: the comparison of local sensor data against interface-received data.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall perform correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies the specific event that triggers the use case: a 'correlation request' received from another unit.

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered when C2 JUs recognize that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (recognition of eligibility) that initiates the automatic correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is when a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly defines the event (recognition of eligibility) and the actor (C² JU) that initiates the resolution process described in the document.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found, the C2 JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the main flow action when track correlation fails — integrating data into the surveillance database as the default system response.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the main flow step following decorrelation: initiating a new surveillance track report with local data and assigning a new track number.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the first step of the main flow for track correlation: the comparison of local and remote data to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they shall be deemed a tentative correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first step of the main flow where the system identifies a potential match after initial testing.

evidence_cards.content: The same two tracks shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the mandatory second verification step required to confirm the tentative correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they shall be processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final action in the successful main flow sequence where the tracks are resolved.

evidence_cards.content: The process of correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data, e.g., position, velocity, boost indication, etc., with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the core action performed by C2 JU to resolve dual designations in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: In order to eliminate dual designations, it is imperative that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represent a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the required state change/outcome of the correlation process (single data point representation).

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the initiating action step in the main flow after recognition of eligibility.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system communication action required in the main flow to propagate correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the content of the correlation request message as part of the canonical interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the expected system response from receiving IUs under normal (non-exceptional) conditions in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A manual capability shall be provided to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f, the correlation restrictions in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g, or the requirements in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a legal alternative path (Manual Correlation) that diverges from the standard automatic testing flow described in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are the specific constraints defining when the manual correlation alternative flow is prohibited.

evidence_cards.content: If the speed of either track is less than 10 dmh, 'course differential' shall not be applied in the correlation test.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow condition where a standard correlation test (course differential) is skipped under specific circumstances (low speed), allowing correlation to proceed without that constraint — a legal variant path diverging from the main flow’s full test application.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with TQ less than or equal to e are not eligible for correlation, except for new local real-time tracks (see paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f(1)(a) and 4.4.4.3.1f(4)).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an exception-based eligibility rule that creates an alternative flow: normally restricted tracks (TQ ≤ e) can still enter correlation if they are new local real-time tracks — a divergence from the default exclusion path.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction preventing automatic correlation, the operator shall be alerted to take action, such as changing the local ID/Exercise Indicator or transmitting an ID Difference Report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow where the main flow's automatic progression is halted by a specific condition (conflicting IDs), requiring operator intervention to resolve the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: An exception to the automatic correlation restrictions allows correlation if one track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile and the other has an ID of Friend, permitting the breaking of an engagement or destruction of a missile in flight.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a specific alternative path that overrides standard restrictions (like ID conflicts or Operational Contingency Constraints) to allow correlation in critical tactical situations.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific alternative path where the correlation process is halted due to conflicting constraints on both tracks, rather than proceeding to resolution.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow where the receiving unit proposes swapping the retained/dropped track designations instead of accepting the originator's proposal.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and the Dropped TN has an OCC: if RV is set to 0, transmit a reverse correlation with RV set to 1; if RV is set to 1, transmit a correlation rejection with RV set to 2; if RV is set to 3, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines alternative successful flows for handling specific state mismatches (Retained vs Dropped TN) during correlation requests.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific action sequence for the 'reverse correlation' alternative flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the Dropped TN does not have an OCC, execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow condition based on the absence of an Operational Contingency Constraint (OCC).

evidence_cards.content: The J7.2 Correlation message shall not be inhibited by any filter.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a constraint on the main flow's transmission step (Step 6), ensuring that even when filters are active, the correlation request message is always allowed to transmit — thus defining an alternative path where filtering does not block resolution.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific inhibiting conditions (exceptions) that prevent the successful completion of a manual correlation request, forcing the system to reject the operation.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a strict temporal boundary condition for the correlation process; exceeding this limit likely invalidates the test data or triggers an error state in the correlation logic.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation; (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed; (c) Confirm the restriction, thereby inhibiting the correlation; or (d) Conduct voice coordination to resolve the situation.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific exception flow when conflicting IDs prevent automatic correlation, requiring operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the timeout exception condition that terminates the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system response (message transmission) for the exception condition of rejecting a correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the recovery constraint (time-based inhibition) following an exception/rejection event.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R^2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific cleanup action taken by the originating unit regarding the dropped track data in the context of the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the temporal boundary condition that triggers an exception state if the test is delayed beyond this limit.

evidence_cards.content: A track with TQ ≤ e shall not be tested for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific prohibition condition where the correlation test is explicitly barred, constituting an exception flow to the main correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with Qpg = 0 shall not be tested for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific prohibition condition based on data quality flags where the correlation test is explicitly barred.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks of different E/C (Environment/Category) shall not be tested for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a restriction preventing correlation testing between tracks with incompatible environment or category attributes.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with existing E/C conflicts shall not be tested for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies an existing conflict state that acts as a barrier to initiating the correlation test.

evidence_cards.content: Simulated tracks shall not be tested for correlation with live tracks, and live tracks shall not be tested with simulated tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a hard constraint prohibiting cross-correlation between simulation and operational (live) data streams.

evidence_cards.content: If the Altitude Source of either track is 0 (No Statement/Estimated) or 2 (Aircraft Report), Altitude shall not be used in the correlation test.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception condition where a specific data field (Altitude) is excluded from the correlation test based on source quality, which constitutes an exception flow branch for handling incomplete or unreliable altitude data during correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if the local/remote data held indicates that both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks (i.e., being updated with local positional data).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific condition where automatic correlation is restricted/blocked, constituting an exception flow.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement, even if the other track has Strength greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception to the restriction regarding Strength field values, allowing correlation to proceed despite one track having high strength.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or Exercise Indicator and ID, (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, (c) Confirm the restriction (inhibiting correlation), or (d) Conduct voice coordination.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception flow for handling ID conflicts during correlation, including operator intervention options.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request, and all associated processing shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the timeout condition and failure outcome for the correlation execution process.

evidence_cards.content: When an ID conflict exists (an ID difference that cannot be automatically accepted or rejected), the differences must be presented to operators for evaluation and may require voice coordination for final resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception handling path for conflicting IDs, specifying the operator intervention and voice coordination required when automatic processing fails.

evidence_cards.content: Receipt of ID data on a TN for which the receiving JU does not have R² and local positional data is not held will automatically be accepted and the remote ID placed in the database for retention.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific recovery/acceptance behavior for an exception case involving missing local data (R² and positional data).

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the exception handling path (operator alert and voice coordination) when a manual correlation request is rejected, which is part of the exception_flow for resolving dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies that for automatic correlation rejections, providing an operator alert is optional (a system option), defining a variant exception response behavior.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific constraint (time-based inhibition) following a correlation rejection exception, preventing immediate retry of the same correlation pair.

evidence_cards.content: If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a condition (both tracks having Operational Contingency Constraints) that forces a correlation rejection, representing an exception flow trigger.

evidence_cards.content: There is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 1; in this case, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines another specific exception condition (OCC on Dropped TN combined with RV=1) that mandates correlation rejection.

evidence_cards.content: The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; in which case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This lists Environment/Category mismatch or conflict as a restriction causing correlation rejection, an exception flow condition.

evidence_cards.content: One track is simulated and the other is live; in which case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies a mix of simulated and live tracks as a condition forcing correlation rejection, an exception flow trigger.

evidence_cards.content: Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; in which case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies that if both tracks are locally derived real-time, correlation is rejected, defining another exception condition.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R^2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception handling path where the system must transmit a rejection message (RV=1) instead of accepting the correlation when a conflict exists with another JU's ownership.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R^2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific exception logic based on data quality (Geodetic Position Quality = 0) that overrides the standard acceptance behavior, resulting in discarding the PPLI message.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not received for the dropped Track Number (TN) after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request, the correlation is deemed to have failed and all associated processing shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific time-based exception condition leading to failure and cancellation of the process.

evidence_cards.content: If the own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted. If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after this transmission, the own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception flow where specific data possession ($R^2$) alters the standard drop procedure and imposes a mandatory delay (inhibition) on re-attempting correlation.

evidence_cards.content: When a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow where automatic correlation is halted due to conflicting Operational Contingency Constraints (OCC) on both tracks.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response and inhibition logic following a correlation rejection exception.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R^2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific handling path for resolving dual designations when the originator retains responsibility for the dropped track.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the recovery action (voice coordination) required when a manual correlation attempt fails.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs rejecting the requested correlation shall initiate transmission of a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory message response format for a correlation rejection exception.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation is deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received for the Dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the timeout condition that results in a failure state rather than a successful postcondition.

evidence_cards.content: If the own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track upon successful correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific state change for the Retained TN when the Dropped TN was held locally.

evidence_cards.content: If the own unit has R squared data for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted for the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system action required to resolve the dual designation when remote data is involved.

evidence_cards.content: If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0 Drop Track message, the own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-correlation state and inhibition constraint regarding the dropped track.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful correlation, the originating C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message to drop the Dropped TN if it holds R^2 data for that track.
